body:
Trivially correct under the assumptions that the operators used in `VariantUtilityFunctions::type_convert()` cover all the cases that `Variant::construct()` covered  (i.e. the list in `Variant::_register_variant_constructors()` whereby `VariantConstructor<To,From>` are both types that can be represented in `Variant`) **and** vice versa. Otherwise, it's not just a simple shortcut.

As far as I can tell, the operators used in `type_convert()` are actually capable of more than the constructors used in `construct()`, for example:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/81ab961f91066a63bcbf3ec340962bb1a1ada558/core/variant/variant.cpp#L1777-L1793
has more options for the `From` type than the constructors do:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4d10419cacd6d3009976e8f9fd3abd970fd58018/core/variant/variant_construct.cpp#L84-L87

However, thanks to the `if (Variant::can_convert_strict(p_variant.get_type(), variant_type))` gating, these looser operator conversions will not be used, meaning no change in behavior is expected. 

Furthermore, in the future, this does mean that we may be able to expand the conversion range for container types (for example downcasting `Vector3` into `Vector2(x,y)`) if so desired.
